subtitle: See it · understand it · try it

sections.title: Meet the bicycle
sections.lookPrompt: Can you spot the wheels and the pedals?

beats.label: WHEELS
beats.text: A bicycle is a vehicle with wheels. The wheels roll along the ground.

beats.label: RIDER POWER
beats.text: Your feet push the pedals. That is how the rider gives the bicycle power.

sections.remember: The rider gives the bicycle its power.
sections.childPrompt: Point to both wheels. Now point to the pedals.

sections.title: Each part has a job
sections.visualLabel: A bicycle showing its main parts
sections.lookPrompt: Find a part that helps the bicycle go, turn, or stop.

beats.label: GO
beats.text: Wheels roll. Your feet push the pedals.

beats.label: TURN AND STOP
beats.text: Turn the handlebar to steer. Use the brakes to slow down.

beats.label: USEFUL EXTRAS
beats.text: A bell and a carrier are useful extras. Some bicycles have them and some do not.

sections.remember: Different bicycle parts do different jobs.
sections.childPrompt: Choose one part. Say its name and its job.

sections.title: Follow what happens next
sections.lookPrompt: Start at the pedals. What moves next?

beats.label: MAKE IT GO
beats.text: One push starts a chain of movement.

sections.remember: One action can start the next action.
sections.childPrompt: Trace the GO chain with your finger. Then trace the SLOW chain.

sections.title: One word can do two jobs
sections.visualLabel: A bicycle with its pedal area emphasised
sections.lookPrompt: Look at pedal. Can it name a thing and an action?

beats.label: PEDAL
beats.text: Pedal can name a part. It can also tell an action.

beats.label: BRAKE
beats.text: Brake can name a part. It can also tell an action.

sections.remember: Some words can do more than one job.
sections.childPrompt: Make two tiny sentences with pedal: one thing, one action.

sections.title: Hear the sound pattern
sections.visualLabel: A cat used for the short-a sound
sections.lookPrompt: Say cat, cap, and map slowly. Listen to the middle sound.

beats.label: SHORT A
beats.text: Cat, cap, and map all have the same short-a sound in the middle.

beats.label: A OR AN?
beats.text: Listen to the first sound when you choose a or an.

sections.remember: Listen to the sound at the start of the word.
sections.childPrompt: Say cat, cap, map. Then say: a bicycle, a helmet, an apple.

sections.title: Put the clues in order
sections.lookPrompt: Read the three actions. Which happens first?

beats.label: TINY STORY
beats.text: Ria fastens her helmet. She checks the brakes. Then she begins to pedal.

beats.label: ORDER CLUES
beats.text: Words like then and last help tell the order. Actions can also help us understand simple reasons.

sections.remember: Find the actions, then put them in order.
sections.childPrompt: Tell the tiny story in three steps: first, next, last.

sections.title: Three checks before you ride
sections.visualLabel: A bicycle, helmet, and safety check
sections.lookPrompt: Before riding, what should you check?

beats.label: 1 · HELMET
beats.text: Fasten a properly fitted cycling helmet before you ride.

beats.label: 2 · BIKE CHECK
beats.text: Check that the brakes work and that the tyres are ready.

beats.label: 3 · BELL
beats.text: A bicycle bell can tell others that a rider is nearby.

sections.childPrompt: Say the three checks aloud: helmet, brakes, tyres.
